title: Kernel rigidity for a flat target with no extra closed-fibre equations
statement: Let R,A,T be local commutative rings, T Noetherian, and B a commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let q:R -> A be a surjective local map, f:A -> B flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], j:R -> T local, and v:T -> B surjective. Suppose v j=f q and ker v is contained in m_R T. Then ker v=(ker q)T. Neither regularity, completeness, flatness of j, nor a power-series presentation is required.

source.place: Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) implies (3), compatible presentation through the displayed isomorphism S tensor_R A -> B; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NQ.

proof.text: Commutativity gives K=(ker q)T contained in ker v. Locality puts K in m_T, so D=T/K is Noetherian local. The proven quotient-kernel equivalence R/ker q ≃ A defines the induced map A -> D. The descended surjection D -> B is A-linear, and its kernel lies in m_A D by q's surjective maximal-ideal image and the hypothesis on ker v.

Apply Mathlib LinearMap.ker_inf_smul_top_eq_smul_of_flat to the A-linear descended surjection: its target B is flat over A. Since the kernel is contained in m_A D, the intersection on the left is the kernel itself. Ideal.smul_restrictScalars rewrites the right as the product of the D-ideal m_A D with the kernel.

The kernel is finitely generated over D, and m_A D lies in m_D because A -> D is local. Nakayama gives zero kernel of D -> B. Its injectivity says that each element of ker v dies already in T/K, proving ker v contained in K. Together with the initial inclusion this gives equality.
